task_name: Pressing gate 1: the state line, the commit, the push and the pull request

rubric.result: The objective promises five things and each one has lines behind it in freeze-spec.ts. Writes `**Estado:** CONGELADA` with today's date: `const on = EpicSpec.dateOf(this.now())` and `this.specs.rewrite({ root, spec, text: spec.frozenAt(on) })`, where `EpicSpec#frozenAt` rewrites both the state line and `**Fecha de congelación:**`. Commits the spec and its design document: `this.branch.publish({ root, paths: [design, spec.path], message })`. Pushes the epic's branch: the same `publish`, whose port answers the branch it pushed. Opens its pull request: `this.pullRequests.open({ repository, branch, title, body })` on the branch `publish` answered. Answers both: `new SpecFrozen({ outcome: FROZEN, findings: [], on, pullRequest })`. Nothing the objective names is missing.

Both tests the TDD line names are in the diff with the assertions it wrote down. `it('a spec with a pending clarification marker is refused and nothing is written, committed, pushed or opened')` asserts `frozen.outcome` is `FreezeOutcome.NOT_FREEZABLE`, `frozen.findings` equals exactly one `FreezeFinding({ code: CLARIFICATION_MARKER, line: 9, detail: '- [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: who commits the freeze?]' })` — line 9 is where the mother puts that line — and that `rewriteAsked`, `publishAsked` and `openAsked` are all empty, which is the 'never asked' the line demands. Its boundary pair `it('writes the state line with today date, commits both documents, pushes and opens the pull request')` fixes `now` at `new Date(2026, 8, 14)`, asserts the text handed to `rewrite` is the frozen document carrying `**Estado:** CONGELADA` and `**Fecha de congelación:** 2026-09-14`, that `publish` got `paths: [Mother.DESIGN_PATH, Mother.PATH]` with the design first, and that `open` got `branch: Mother.BRANCH`, which is what the branch double answers from `publish`. Same assertion, same input, same expected value as the sentence.

The Contract block is stated name by name in the diff. `FreezeSpecParams` has `readonly root: CheckoutRoot` and `readonly repository: RepositoryName` and the constructor takes the object named `asked`, exactly as written. `FreezeOutcome` is `Object.freeze({ FROZEN: 'frozen', NO_SPEC: 'no-spec', ALREADY_FROZEN: 'already-frozen', NOT_FREEZABLE: 'not-freezable' } as const)` — the four literal values of the block. `SpecFrozen` declares `outcome`, `findings`, `on` and `pullRequest` with the block's types. `FreezeSpec`'s constructor takes `{ specs, branch, pullRequests, now }` and `execute(params: FreezeSpecParams): Promise<SpecFrozen>`. The prescribed order holds and stops at the first refusal: `mostRecent` null -> NO_SPEC, `isFrozen()` -> ALREADY_FROZEN, `!isFreezable()` -> NOT_FREEZABLE carrying `spec.findings()`, `design()` null -> `throw new EpicSpecNotUnderstood(...)`, and only then `dateOf`/`rewrite`/`publish`/`open`. The three composed texts match the brief character for character: `Freeze the execution spec of ${title} (${on})`, `${title} — design and execution spec`, and the three-part body ending `Control Tower's gate 1 wrote the state line and committed both. The groom stays refused until this pull request merges.` The ports it drives exist with these exact signatures (`epic-specs.ts#rewrite`, `epic-branch.ts#publish`, `pull-requests.ts#open`).

Rows the diff bears on, each implemented with the row's value. D-10: both files are `.ts` under `backend/`. D-11: whether the spec is freezable is asked of `EpicSpec#isFreezable()`, which delegates to the plugin's `analyzeSpecFreeze`; the diff grows no second opinion — there is no marker scan, no hypothesis check and no threshold anywhere in freeze-spec.ts. D-13: nothing is stored; `on` is computed from the injected `now` on the call and the only write is the spec's own state line, which D-23 asks for. D-23: after the state line the use case publishes — `branch.publish` then `pullRequests.open` with both documents named in the body. D-7: nothing in the diff merges or writes to a pull request after opening it; `PullRequests#open` is the only pull-request call. D-16: cmux is not named. D-22 is the route's half (Task 7/8) and this use case neither weakens nor anticipates it. Every other row the diff leaves alone.

EXEMPLARS: against `application/actions/open-coordinating-session.ts`, `FreezeSpec` takes its collaborators through the constructor by name and drives them in order; against `application/queries/read-implementation-progress.ts` and its sibling `read-spec-freeze.ts` it declares params object, closed vocabulary and result object in the same module in the same order, with `Object.freeze(this)` on the immutable ones. The test follows `__tests__/application/open-coordinating-session.test.ts` and `read-spec-freeze.test.ts` exactly: doubles that extend the real ports, a `Mother` of named scenarios, a `Flow` that assembles them and runs the use case. ARCHITECTURE: a mutation lives in `application/actions` (the layout `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` fixes); the module imports only `domain/ports` and `domain/value-objects` — no infrastructure — so the direction of dependencies holds; no suffix on the type, its params or its result; the result object is declared beside the use case. TESTING: application layer with every port doubled, assertions on what each port received and what the use case returned, values (EpicSpec, CheckoutRoot, RepositoryName) real and not doubled, no prose, names that are sentences. Read for `an assertion is not finished until it has been seen to fail`: each of the five could fail for the reason its name gives — in particular `a spec that names no design document raises instead of publishing half the epic` uses a mother that IS freezable (`## Hipótesis` with its bet, no marker), so it really reaches the `design() === null` branch instead of being refused earlier. DEFECTS.MD, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — `FreezeOutcome` is a frozen vocabulary with its `FreezeOutcomeValue` type and the answer carries a member, not a boolean; there is no dispatch over it in this diff, so no catch-all to check; complies. (2) raw map as the return value of logic — the use case answers `SpecFrozen`, a declared immutable result object; the object literals handed to `rewrite`, `publish` and `open` are those ports' own declared parameter shapes, not maps returned by logic; complies. (3) two fields that have to agree — `on: string | null` and `pullRequest: ReviewedPullRequest | null` carry the absence in the type, with no sentinel (no empty string, no epoch date); `outcome` is not a flag repeating another field, because `NO_SPEC` and `ALREADY_FROZEN` are indistinguishable from the other three fields and only the vocabulary tells them apart; the four-field shape is the brief's Contract verbatim; complies. (4) an error named for what happens — `EpicSpecNotUnderstood`, of the existing `SpecFreezeFailure` family, is named for what happened and not for the module that raised it; complies. STYLE: no comment or docstring, every identifier and every composed text in English, every function hangs off a type. BOUNDARIES/DELIVERY: no document of either yardstick prescribes a shape of delivery for a new use case with no public contract altered — the module is new, no existing signature or call site changes — so the diff complies as it stands. TWO CLASHES DECLARED AND LEFT OUT OF THE FINDINGS: (a) the `test-driven-development` skill says of a test name `'and' in name? Split it`, and both prescribed names carry one — but the plan wrote them verbatim in **TDD:** and **Tests:**, so splitting them would fail `asercion-tdd`; the defect is the plan's. (b) `type ReviewedPullRequest = { readonly number: number, readonly url: string }` is declared locally for the fourth time in `src/` — but `domain/ports/pull-requests.ts` does not export it and exporting it would touch a file outside this task's **Files:**; it is also the repo's standing idiom (7 files before this diff, including the exemplars `pull-requests.ts`, `gh-pull-requests.ts` and `read-spec-freeze.ts`).

Does not apply: no pre-existing test lost anything. Both backend files are `new file mode 100644`, so their test file has no `-` lines at all. The only `-` lines in the whole diff are the two prose lines of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-14-issue-329-gate-1-the-freeze.md`, which are plan narrative about Task 5's coverage and not an assertion, a case or a test.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code. Every composed text the test asserts on — the frozen document, the commit message, the pull request title and the six-line body — is built in `backend/src/application/actions/freeze-spec.ts` and in `EpicSpec#frozenAt`/`#dateOf`, and the test only names the literal it expects. The scaffolding (`EpicSpecsDouble`, `EpicBranchDouble`, `PullRequestsDouble`) records what it was asked and answers fixed values; no branch of the flow lives there. Reverting the two production symbols leaves the test unable to import `FreezeSpec`, and the refusal ordering, the date format and the body text have no second home in the test file.

Inside the two declared files, every line traces to a sentence of the task: the use case is the **Objective:** and the ordered prose, the five tests are **TDD:** and **Tests:**, and nothing else was added — no helper, no rename, no adjacent fix, and nothing that touches `groom.js`, `slices.js`, the brainstorming skill, the groom, the merge or the existing endpoints that `### Out of scope` names. The third path is the plan file, which is an amendment and is ruled here: the hunk replaces one sentence of Task 5's prose, which claimed Task 5 brought `EpicSpec#isFreezable()` under test, with the true statement that it does not and that Task 6 covers it. I checked the claim against the tree: `read-spec-freeze.ts` calls `isFrozen()`, `findings()` and `frozenOn()` and never `isFreezable()`, while this diff calls it and drives it both ways. The amendment removes no route from any **Files:**, no test name from any **Tests:**, no assertion from any **TDD:** and weakens no **Verification:** command; it disarms nothing and it makes the committed record true. It is still a line no sentence of Task 6 asks for, which is the low finding below; no repair is asked, because reverting it would restore a falsehood a previous judge already reported.

Five new tests, all three properties held. Deterministic: the only clock is injected — `Mother.TODAY = () => new Date(2026, 8, 14)` — and `EpicSpec.dateOf` reads local components of that fixed date, so `2026-09-14` comes out in any timezone; no network, no filesystem, no randomness, no sleep. Isolated: each test builds its own `Flow` with fresh doubles through `Flow.freezing(...)`, the mother's statics are frozen values and specs are rebuilt per call, nothing is shared mutably and no test depends on the order of the file. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on what the use case returned (`outcome`, `findings`, `on`, `pullRequest`) or on what a port received (`rewriteAsked`, `publishAsked`, `openAsked` with their literal payloads) — never on a double's call count as a proxy — and none of them survives reverting `freeze-spec.ts`. The `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` skill loaded; the one thing it gave that bears here is `Minimal | One thing. 'and' in name? Split it`, and the two names that carry an `and` are the plan's own literal text, which is the clash declared under `patrones` and not a finding against this diff.

findings.what: The diff carries a hunk in the plan that no sentence of Task 6 asks for: it rewrites Task 5's prose about which domain method that task brought under test. Ruled a justified amendment and no repair is asked — the new sentence is true (`read-spec-freeze.ts` never calls `isFreezable()`, this task does and covers both its answers), it removes no route, no test name and no verification command, and its proper home, Task 5's commit, was already sealed by the run machine. Recorded only so the out-of-task line is visible in the count.
